page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with a running head at the top and the page number at top right. No margin notes. Below the text: a signature at bottom left and a catchword at bottom right.

main_text.head: Aliud.
main_text.p: L.maximum vitium.C.de liberis prȩterit.[?] probatur fœmineam successionem in militaribus beneficiis quoque justam esse.
main_text.head: Responsio.
main_text.p: Allegans autoritatem juris impertinenter, id est, extra causam, minime gentium censetur aliquid demonstrare: qua infractione utitur Jureconsultus Oldendorpius.
main_text.head: Aliud.
main_text.p: Lactantius: Tanta est autoritas vetustatis, ut inquirere in eam scelus esse dicatur. Quo fit, ut Justinianus venerandam vocet. Et proverbiale est: Sapientes sunt, qui veteri vino utuntur: Veterum igitur dogmatis seu placitis omnino standum.
main_text.head: Responsio.
main_text.p: Autoritas humana cedit rationi. Et error vetustatis, (qui evidenter ostendendus est) non prajudicat veritati.
main_text.head: Aliud.
main_text.p: Speculator vel Baldus juris interpres hoc dicit: Ergo pro jure tenendum.
main_text.head: Responsio.
main_text.p: Antecessoribus juris creditur, non quia responderunt & asseruerunt, sed quia ex jure & æquitate responderunt & asseruerunt. Non tam autores in disputando, quam rationis momenta quærenda sunt, ait Cicero, de

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "prȩterit" (the ligature in "præterit" is hard to read; marked [?]); "prajudicat" may be "præjudicat" with a worn ligature. The "Responsio." labels are printed in italic type and are set apart on their own lines, so they are given as level 3 headings. The text "Nat." at the foot is a catchword. The signature "D 5" is partly worn. Spelling of "prajudicat" and "justam" follows the scan with long s as s.
